routes.approach: This supplier comes first in dependency order. The connected statement matches the latest translator candidate accepted by all three reviewers. Theorem 6.7, archived p. 26 and current published p. 28, quantifies over every bimodule map at the fixed boundary. Keep the existential index type and the separate finite-combination iff. The earlier reviewer objection about losing the drawn indexed scope applies to the displayed left-diagram instance. All three reviews of the intervening supported-orbit-only candidate rejected the extra index and weight constraints on the general theorem. The accepted candidate uses PointwiseIndexedDrawing for the existential sum and an IndexedDrawing evaluator for the finite list, with no required shape equality in the finite clause. Keep independent finite complex labels at the lower mixed projection, middle parallel induction crossing, and upper mixed multiplication, and finite fibers for each lower projection parameter. The horizontal map operations are complex-bilinear and the bimodules tensor over the common group algebra. Use the supported orbit subtype and its matrix coefficients as witnesses. The projected-stabilizer indicator supplies each summand, and orbit_columns extends the finite column supports to general inputs. For the finite iff, use indexed_fold only to compare evaluations with the installed finite-label converse. The engine registered the exact reviewed source after compilation and an audit reporting propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

routes.approach: The engine compiled, audited, and registered the exact Example 6.6 replay after its scheduled inputs were ready. Its displayed identity is on archived p. 27 and current published p. 29. Carry forward the checked local declarations rigid_eq, support_atBoundary, fixed_right_code, right_all_support, finite_right_sum, right_column, and pointwise_column_sum from the exact-statement replay. The rigidity and support lemmas transport across the boundary reorderings and cover every PlanarAtBoundary witness. The named-family finite iff in ExpansionIntoRightDiagrams has a narrower drawing predicate. The replay proves the obstruction by taking x outside the union of the lower label supports in a finite combination. The left column is then nonzero while the finite sum vanishes. Each selected column of the infinite family equals the left column, and the pointwise-support proof extends to all inputs with the index P fixed. Keep the finite obstruction as an equality test on evaluated combinations. The replay specializes EvaluationWithOneProjection at the named left drawing and named right family, then proves the broader support bound by typed syntax induction.
